candidate_findings.title: FileSafe is not explicitly re-run after argument mutation
candidate_findings.gap: The authoritative order performs FileSafe before provider normalization and arg-touching hooks, while the only explicit post-hook recheck names permission and schema.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A normalizer or hook can change a previously checked path or shell argument before dispatch, allowing the executed target to differ from the FileSafe-approved target.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: No mandatory FileSafe recheck is named after every path-affecting normalization or hook mutation, and no contract binds the checked canonical target to the target actually dispatched.

evidence_refs.excerpt: 3. For file-affecting tools, run FileSafe/write-scope checks on the normalized path arguments.

4. Apply provider-specific argument normalizers where the tool surface explicitly allows them, including concrete compatibility fixes such as GLM quoted-JSON unquoting and Qwen XML-wrapper stripping before schema validation.
7. Re-run permission and schema validation if hook output changed arguments.

- **FileSafe contract:** FileSafe exposes e.g. `check_bash_command(cmd)`, `check_write_path(path)`, `check_read_path(path)`. For file-affecting or shell-affecting tools, FileSafe runs on normalized arguments inside the canonical `§8.2` flow; hook-mutated arguments trigger the required re-checks before dispatch.

candidate_findings.title: Ask permissions can become executable provider grants before approval
candidate_findings.gap: Claude and Copilot derivation places allow and ask tools into executable CLI allowlists, while DAE providers execute tools themselves and post-run reconciliation occurs only after execution.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An ask-class mutation can execute before Puppet Master obtains approval, and post-run reconciliation cannot undo an external side effect.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The capsule lacks a provider-by-mode enforcement matrix showing how ask remains non-executable before approval, and lacks a concrete eligibility oracle proving that each DAE provider can enforce the resolved restriction pre-spawn.

evidence_refs.excerpt: | Claude | Build `--allowedTools "Read,Edit,Bash"` from tools that are allow or ask (ask still needs runtime approval). Omit any tool that is deny. |
| Copilot | Build `--allow-tool '...'` list from allow+ask; build `--deny-tool '...'` from deny. If all allow, can use `--allow-all-tools` and only pass `--deny-tool` for denied. |

HTE / DAE split (canonical): the "before forwarding" wording above applies to **HTE** only, where Puppet Master remains the tool executor. In **DAE**, the provider executes tools inside a jail, so enforcement relies on deterministic pre-spawn restriction + post-run reconciliation. Providers that cannot support that restriction path MUST NOT advertise `dae_allowed = true`.

candidate_findings.title: Flattened MCP names are not collision-safe
candidate_findings.gap: The underscore concatenation format is not injective when server slugs or tool names can themselves contain underscores.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two distinct server/tool tuples can resolve to the same permission key, causing wildcard or per-tool authority to apply to the wrong tool.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The capsule supplies no component grammar, escaping rule, tuple-level identity, collision rejection behavior, or migration behavior for an existing collision.

evidence_refs.excerpt: MCP tool names use the owner-defined underscore-only format `{server_slug}_{tool_name}`.

candidate_findings.title: MCP unavailable classification can turn terminal causes into transient failures
candidate_findings.gap: Auth loss and schema mismatch can create the unavailable state, but unavailable calls default to provider_transient unless an undefined stricter classification is selected, while both causes are declared terminal for retry.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A higher layer can retry an invocation that the retry contract says must be terminal, producing loops, repeated prompts, or unnecessary reconnects.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: No deterministic cause-to-failure-class table defines the class for startup timeout, transport failure, auth loss, schema mismatch, and health-check failure.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - auth-required, permission-denied, schema-mismatch, validation-failed, content-filter, and safety-stop classes are terminal for that invocation and MUST NOT be retried automatically
When an MCP server is unavailable because of startup timeout, transport failure, auth loss, schema mismatch, or repeated health-check failure, PM treats this as a structured degraded-state condition.
- Calls to those tools fail immediately with a structured error and `failure_class=provider_transient` (or a stricter class when the error is known-fatal).

candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: No precedence rule distinguishes temporary hiding from visible unavailability or defines the exact registry and GUI transition for startup failure versus transient list failure.

candidate_findings.title: Retry cap and minimum-delay boundary are not executable deterministically
candidate_findings.gap: The text does not state whether the three automatic attempts include the initial dispatch, despite listing three backoff bases, and it clamps a provider minimum delay to the remaining budget without defining whether a too-short retry executes or terminates.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can perform different numbers of side-effecting calls or violate Retry-After/provider throttling requirements.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Attempt numbering, initial-versus-retry accounting, backoff-to-attempt mapping, deterministic jitter algorithm/serialization, and the nonzero-budget-but-below-minimum transition are absent.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - transient transport, server-warming, and recoverable bootstrap failures MAY retry automatically, but the total automatic attempts are capped at 3 per invocation

- default backoff bases are `1000ms`, `2000ms`, then `4000ms`; jitter is applied as `clamp(base_ms + deterministic_jitter_ms, 0ms, parent_remaining_budget_ms)` where `deterministic_jitter_ms` is selected from the closed interval `[-floor(base_ms * 0.25), +floor(base_ms * 0.25)]` using the invocation id plus attempt number as the seed; a stricter `Retry-After` or provider minimum delay raises the post-jitter floor before the parent-budget clamp
- if the remaining budget is exhausted before a retry starts, PM emits a structured timeout or budget result without dispatching the new attempt

candidate_findings.title: Similarity-based loop suppression lacks a test oracle
candidate_findings.gap: Near-match signatures, substantial equivalence, and progress are normative decision inputs without algorithms or thresholds.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: One implementation can suppress a useful recovery attempt while another loops on effectively identical failures.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Canonical normalization, target identity, signature construction, similarity threshold, progress evidence, collision behavior, and diagnostic fields are not defined.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - automatic retry suppression compares normalized tool fingerprint, canonical target, error class/status, and near-match argument or stderr signatures; same or substantially equivalent failures without progress MUST stop further retries and emit a diagnostic instead of looping indefinitely

candidate_findings.title: Shell safety depends on an undefined cross-shell scanning grammar
candidate_findings.gap: Fallback full-string scanning is allowed across Bash, cmd.exe, and PowerShell, but the accepted and rejected grammar is not defined for quoting, expansion, encoded newlines, here-documents, process substitution, environment indirection, aliases, or shell-specific metacharacters.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A parser/scanner mismatch can miss an executable construct or reject a harmless quoted construct, and path escaping can differ from the shell's command parsing.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The capsule lacks a normative shell-family grammar, normalization stage, quote ownership model for the command passed to `-c`, and cross-platform adversarial acceptance corpus.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - banned-command checks scan the full rendered command string, including metacharacter and control forms such as `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, subshell/grouping constructs, command substitution (`$()` and backticks), and redirection operators where relevant to the shell family; this is full-string validation for the shell-runtime surface

- implementations SHOULD prefer structured parsing or AST-aware validation where the shell family makes it practical; fallback scanning still MUST evaluate the full rendered command rather than only the first token

- Unix-style shell dispatch passes the already `shellQuote`-protected command through `exec.Command("bash", "-c", command)` or an equivalent one-layer platform runner; it must not run a second interpreter after quoting.
- shell selection is platform-aware (`/bin/bash` or equivalent on Unix; `cmd.exe` / PowerShell family on Windows based on configured tool semantics)

- all paths interpolated into shell commands MUST be shell-escaped for the target platform; on Windows this means quoting, double-backslash handling, or forward-slash conversion according to the selected shell, and individual tools MUST NOT implement their own competing escaping layer

candidate_findings.title: Shell isolation and non-blocking queue states are incomplete
candidate_findings.gap: Isolation is scoped per agent tree while claiming no leakage across agent boundaries, and non-blocking queues have no capacity, overflow, ordering, fairness, cancellation, restart, or teardown semantics.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Sibling or parent/child agents may observe shared environment state, and load or shell death races may drop, reorder, starve, or duplicate commands.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The shell ownership key, environment clone/reset boundary, queue state machine, backpressure result, pending-write fate on death, and restart generation behavior are absent.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - shell instances are isolated per agent tree so environment variables do not leak across session/agent boundaries
- shell lifecycle is mutex-guarded; work queues MUST be `/non-blocking`, and writes to a dead shell return a structured error instead of hanging forever
- `OC-LIFE-006` requires an alive-check before queue writes; if the shell is dead, PM returns a structured LIFE error instead of blocking forever
